chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl, who said:

A slave said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I said to my master, 'Sell me for seven hundred dirhams, and I will give you three hundred dirhams'.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'If you had something on the day you stipulated to give him, then it is upon you to give it; and if you did not have anything on that day, then there is nothing upon you'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave cannot pay the agreed ransom on the stipulated day?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the conditional nature of the *kitabah* (self-purchase) contract, establishing that the slave's debt obligation is contingent upon his actual financial capacity on the due date rather than being an absolute liability. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *al-yamin* (oath/condition) linked to ability, ensuring that the master cannot claim the full amount if the slave was genuinely unable to pay when the condition was set, thereby protecting the slave from perpetual bondage due to temporary insolvency.
